Der Einsatz von Leverage ist gänzlich zu vermeiden. Die Stop-Loss-Niveaus der Positionen im Portfolio sind anhand der technischen Unterstützungspunkte sorgfältig festzulegen, und bei diesen Niveaus ist diszipliniert zu schließen. Das Aufwärtspotenzial hingegen wird auf positive Entwicklungen wie Anzeichen einer Lockerung der Zinserwartungen der Fed oder eine Abnahme der geopolitischen Spannungen begrenzt bleiben. Die Erwartungen an die September-Sitzung der US-Notenbank und ihre Zinsentscheidung wirken sich unmittelbar auf die globalen Liquiditätsbedingungen aus und sind der zentrale Katalysator, der die Risikobereitschaft an den Schwellenmärkten bestimmt. Zwar bewegen sich die Märkte in der Erwartung einer Zinssenkung, doch ein unerwarteter Anstieg der Inflationsdaten könnte dieses Szenario zunichtemachen. Dies könnte die Erwartung einer "Lockerung der finanziellen Bedingungen" für die türkischen Märkte abschwächen und Druck auf die Währung ausüben. Insbesondere der Umstand, dass die Inflationserwartung bei 28,4% verharrt, belastet die Konsumausgaben und die Kostenstrukturen der Unternehmen. Im Inland stützen Schritte wie die zusätzliche Finanzierung von 1,1 Milliarden Dollar für Halkbank zwar den Bankensektor, doch bleibt die Wirkung dieser Unterstützungen auf die langfristige Rentabilität begrenzt. Der Bankensektor erlebt mit den Aktien VAKBN, YKBNK, GARAN, AKBNK und ISCTR einen vollständigen "STARK VERKAUFEN"-Druck. Der Sektor steht unter Druck wegen der Sorge, dass die hohe Inflation die Kreditnachfrage und die Aktivaqualität negativ beeinflusst. Die Höhe des Umlaufvermögens ist ein wichtiger Indikator für die operative Flexibilität und die Marktbeherrschung eines Unternehmens. In diesem Zusammenhang behaupten Holdinggesellschaften wie KCHOL (Koç Holding) und SAHOL (Sabancı Holding) mit riesigen Umlaufvermögen von 3.615 Milliarden TL und 2.790 Milliarden TL ihre Führungsposition in ihren Sektoren. Diese Strukturen erscheinen dank diversifizierter Geschäftsfelder widerstandsfähiger gegenüber einem einzelnen sektoralen Schock. Allerdings geraten Unternehmen aus rohstoffintensiven Sektoren wie Energie und Metall aufgrund der hohen Erdgas- und Energiekosten unter Margendruck. So fällt es Unternehmen wie EREGL (Ereğli Demir Çelik) und SISE (Şişecam) schwer, Kostensteigerungen an die Preise weiterzugeben. Der Bankensektor hingegen versucht in einem Umfeld hoher Inflation und Zinsen, ein Gleichgewicht zwischen Kreditwachstum und Nettozinsmarge herzustellen. In diesem Umfeld treten Banken mit hoher Eigenkapitalquote und starker Liquidität hervor. Die „STARKER VERKAUF“-Signale in der technischen Analyse zeigen jedoch, dass insgesamt eine vorsichtige Herangehensweise an den Bankensektor erforderlich ist. Neben den Finanzkennzahlen bilden die Schuldenstrukturen der Unternehmen und ihre Fremdwährungsverschuldung wesentliche Risikofaktoren gegenüber Wechselkursschwankungen.

Die Vorbereitung eines wirtschaftlichen Maßnahmenpakets Deutschlands gegenüber China und die Spannungen zwischen den USA und China im Bereich der künstlichen Intelligenz erzeugen Unsicherheit in den globalen Handelsströmen. Insbesondere Entwicklungen wie Kürzungen der Sozialhilfe und Anhebungen des Mindestlohns üben Druck auf das Verbrauchervertrauen aus und beeinträchtigen die Dynamik der Binnennachfrage negativ. In diesem Umfeld ist die Anlegerpsychologie in den Verteidigungsmodus übergegangen, und Aktien, die Dividendenpotenzial und Schutz gegen Inflation bieten, treten in den Vordergrund. Diese hohen Realkosten führen dazu, dass das M3-Geldmengenwachstum (im Oktober jährlich %28,65, vorher %29,78) hinter der nominalen Inflation (%29,73) zurückbleibt und sich daher die reale Geldmenge (real M3) kontinuierlich verengt. Die Verengung der realen Geldmenge erodiert — konsistent mit Friedmans These "Inflation ist überall und jederzeit ein monetäres Phänomen" — die Kaufkraft der Gesellschaft und dämpft die Gesamtnachfrage (aggregate demand). Das jährliche Wachstum der Bankkredite um %36,32 (August, vorher %36,60) mag nominal weiterhin hoch erscheinen; jedoch sinkt das reale Kreditwachstum bei Deflationierung mit der Inflation auf einstellige Niveaus (rund %2,3-6). Dies zeigt, dass der Zugang der Unternehmen zu Working-Capital- und Investitionsfinanzierung kostspielig und eingeschränkt geworden ist und die Haushalte die Nutzung von Konsumkrediten (insbesondere Wohnen/Fahrzeug) aufschieben. Die Schrumpfung der Industrieproduktion um monatlich -%1,0 und jährlich -%1,86 sowie das Festkleben der Kapazitätsauslastung bei %74,5 deuten darauf hin, dass die Kombination aus Binnennachfragedruck und externer Nachfrageunsicherheit (EU-Industrie -%1,1) den Investitionsentscheidungsprozess (investment decision) verzögert. en:081c22e64e463792b4f0: Refers to the relationship between the return expected to be obtained from an investment made in any asset or instrument and the risk assumed with the investment made in the said asset or instrument. In principle, there is a positive relationship between the risk assumed and the expected return. Hence, particularly in the financial markets, as the risk assumed increases, the return is expected to increase, and as the risk assumed decreases, the return is expected to decrease. Risk is generally expressed by the standard deviation of the investment's past returns (historical volatility). The expected return from the investment, on the other hand, is the average of the past returns. The risk-return curve formed by the maximum returns that can be obtained in return for a certain risk is called the 'efficient frontier', and its use is particularly for comparison and benchmark purposes.

en:1ec044ec00a58af6e627: In the global macroeconomic picture, the structural divergence between the US and the Euro Zone deepens in the last quarter of 2026, and this divergence affects emerging markets (EM) in different directions through liquidity and risk appetite. The US economy maintained its resilience in the second quarter of 2026 with %2,2 annual growth (quarterly %2,2); however, the engine of this growth is built on the strong course of private consumption expenditures (quarterly %3,2) and the support of retail sales rising %6,3 annually in September. The still-low unemployment rate (%4,2) and the extended unemployment (U-6) at %7,6 levels show that the Fed's "full employment" target is not broken, yet the decline of August JOLTS job openings to 7,079 million and September NFP (29 thousand) falling far below the expectation (90 thousand) indicate that the demand-friendly side is slowly turning supply-friendly. Mixed signals dominate the inflation fight: while headline CPI rose to annual %3,7 (September) and core CPI to %2,6 (September), the Fed's preferred PCE deflator runs at annual %3,4 (August) and core PCE at %3,0 levels. The critical point is September's PPI coming in at monthly %1,3 (annual %6,3), much stronger than expected (monthly %0,5); this indicates that producer cost pressure is still alive and the "last mile" difficulty of inflation continues. The Fed held the policy rate fixed at %4,0 at its October 22 meeting; however, the September dot plot projections (1 year %4,1, 2 years %3,9) exhibited a distinctly "hawkish" shift compared to the previous meeting (%3,6 and %3,4 respectively). This strengthens the possibility that the Fed may postpone the start of its rate-cutting cycle to 2027 or follow a slower pace, even though markets had priced the "soft landing" scenario. The US Treasury yield curve is shaping with this expectation: with 3-month %4,02, 5-year %4,76, 30-year %5,29 levels, the curve is moving away from "bear steepening" dynamics (long-term yields falling less/rising relative to short-term yields) and has begun pricing the risk of long-term real rates staying structurally higher (term premium). The DXY index's relatively calm course at %101,6 levels shows that the Fed's relative hawkishness is offset by the Dollar's reserve currency status and the US growth advantage.

en:20e876a8df2a5b3b8a93: With the aim of increasing domestic savings, diversifying Government Domestic Debt Securities and broadening the investor base, the first Revenue-Indexed Securities (GES) issue was carried out by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance of the Republic of Türkiye on 28 January 2009. In GES issues, returns are indexed to the revenue shares transferred to the budget from the Türkiye Petrolleri Anonim Ortaklığı (TPAO), which has the status of a State Economic Enterprise, the State Supply Office (DMO), the State Airports Authority (DHMİ) and the General Directorate of Coastal Safety (KIYEM). With Revenue-Indexed Securities, an investment instrument has been created whose return is linked to state revenues. Thanks to the minimum coupon payment guarantee to be applied to the said securities, the investor is protected from being adversely affected by the change in the revenue share. Within this framework, in calculating the payments relating to the returns of the said securities, the total of the quarterly and semi-annual revenue shares transferred to the budget by TPAO, DMO, DHMİ and KIYEM is taken as the basis. If the realized revenue collection exceeds the maximum amounts announced in the budget, payment is made to investors based on the counterparts of the said maximum amounts.

en:233befca665aa3bf844a: The use by residents of a country of foreign currency instead of their own national currency as a medium of exchange, unit of account and store of value. Full dollarization is a country's completely abandoning its national currency and adopting a foreign currency as its official currency. Partial dollarization arises when economic units in a country, in an environment of high inflation and uncertainty, begin to prefer financial assets in foreign currency instead of financial assets in national currency, in order to protect themselves from the possible loss of value of the national currency. It is generally observed that the first stage of dollarization develops as 'asset substitution', the beginning of the use of foreign-currency assets as a store of value. On the other hand, the banking crises frequently experienced in the recent past, particularly in emerging markets, have added to the economics literature the concept of 'liability dollarization' in addition to asset dollarization. Liability dollarization is the holding of large amounts of foreign-currency liabilities by all economic units in the country, including the banking and public sectors. Both asset and liability dollarization can be gathered under a single heading and characterized as 'financial dollarization'. Financial dollarization is defined as the tendencies of residents of a country to hold both their assets and their liabilities in foreign currency.

en:50ae4d26c1b035780f51: Today, owing to the importance they carry, particularly for small and open economies, and their potential to directly affect the real economy, exchange rates are used directly as target, indicator or instrument within the framework of the monetary policy implemented. Exchange rate practices take shape between two regimes: the fixed exchange rate regime at one end and free floating at the other. Under a fixed exchange rate regime, the value of the national currency is pegged against a foreign currency or a basket of currencies, and the maintenance of this value is guaranteed by the monetary authority, sometimes explicitly and sometimes implicitly. In Currency Board-type arrangements, while the rate is pegged on the one hand, on the other hand the national money supply is tied entirely to the foreign currency purchases and sales conducted at this rate. Under a free floating exchange rate regime, the price of the exchange rate is determined according to the supply and demand forming in the market. Besides these, many intermediate regimes exist. For example, under a floating regime the rate is largely determined by market supply and demand conditions, but the monetary authority intervenes in the market rarely and in limited amounts; under a managed float regime, again there is no exchange rate target, but interventions can occur frequently for various reasons. Under regimes known as the crawling peg, the rate is guided according to a set of criteria and is intervened in by the monetary authority when necessary. The choice of such exchange rate regimes varies according to the conditions countries find themselves in.

en:7a47ae9146a2d25894e1: The output gap, defined as the difference of the output realized in an economy from its potential level, is an important monetary policy variable in the evaluation of the price pressures in the economy. Under the inflation targeting regime, central banks shape their policies according to the forward-looking inflation expectations rather than realized inflation. Accordingly, in the areas where the output gap is positive, it is estimated that the economy is operating above capacity because of the demand surplus, and that this can cause demand-side inflationary pressure. In contrast, in the areas where the output gap is negative, it is estimated that there is a supply surplus or idle capacity stemming from the weak demand in the economy, and that this too can cause a fall in inflation.

In particular, if the good to be auctioned has no fixed or directly determinable price, or if the seller of the good is unsure about the good's market price, sale by auction eliminates this uncertainty under fully competitive conditions. Auctions can be conducted in different forms. The most common are the multiple-price (Dutch Auction) type auctions in which prices are ordered from largest to smallest, ensuring maximum revenue and minimum cost for the seller. In this auction, the transaction with each participant is made at the price it itself bid. Auctions in which prices are ordered from smallest to largest are called the 'English Auction'. Another auction method is the 'single price' auction. In this auction type, the price at which supply and demand are equated is applied to all the participants winning the auction. In other words, all the transactions are carried out at a single price. Both auction types have advantages and disadvantages relative to one another. In the single price auction, the cost of information gathering is lower and greater participation can be achieved. In the multiple price auction, more intense competition is in question and a lower cost may be in question for the seller. However, all these depend on the structure of the market and the conditions of the day.

Excluding certain items from the index, statistical analysis and model-based methods are frequently used in calculating core inflation; however, the most widely followed core inflation indicators are those obtained by the exclusion method. For this purpose, energy prices, basic food prices and indirect taxes, which are more exposed to external effects (energy prices, seasonal conditions, fiscal policy, etc.) and can be temporary in nature, are the main elements excluded from such inflation calculations. The purpose of using core inflation is to identify the elements that make the change in the general price level persistent. Although the inflation target is set on headline CPI inflation, the course of core inflation indicators is also taken into account so that more realistic policy decisions can be taken. en:b83727ed82edd713fe69: The graphical expression of the relationship, in any time interval, between the various maturities of an investment instrument and the returns at those maturities. The vertical axis holds return/yield, the horizontal axis the maturities. They are classified as positively sloped (normal) yield curves, negatively sloped (inverted) yield curves, flat yield curves and yield curves expressing high returns at medium maturities (bell shape). The movements of the curve over time — its steepening ('steeping': if a positively sloped curve is in question, the distant part of the curve rising and the near part falling, the slope increasing), its flattening ('flattening': in positively sloped yield curves, the distant part falling, the near part rising, the slope decreasing) and the curve moving up or down without changing its shape ('parallel shift') — are so named. An increase in the curve's slope reflects the expectation that interest rates (inflation) will rise in the long term. A decrease in the slope — in other words, the flattening of a positively sloped yield curve (the near side rising, the distant side falling) — expresses investors, with the expectation that interest rates will fall in the future, turning toward the long term in order to benefit from the current interest rates for longer, and hence, with the increasing demand, the return at that maturity falling; and those demanding funds, with the expectation that the opportunity of borrowing at lower interest rates will arise in the future, preferring the short term, and hence, with the excess supply, the return rising.

en:f5627365701c964d4107: The transmission channels of monetary policy to domestic demand (transmission channels) are materializing with the data provided. The "rate corridor" the TCMB forms through its policy rate (%37) and liquidity window rates determines the banking system's cost structure. With the October data, the TL deposit rate runs at %43,04 (previous %43,80), and with the August data the consumer loan rate at %64,74 (previous %63,67); this shows the real deposit rate (taking the annual inflation of %29,73 as base, ~%43,04-11) and the real loan rate (~%27-28) are seriously positive. This high real cost causes M3 money supply growth (annual %28,65 in October, previous %29,78) to lag nominal inflation (%29,73), hence the real money supply (real M3) to contract continuously. The contraction of the real money supply, consistent with Friedman's thesis that "inflation is always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon," erodes society's purchasing power and suppresses aggregate demand. Bank loans growing annually %36,32 (August, previous %36,60) may still look high nominally; however, when deflated by inflation, real credit growth has fallen to single digits (around %2,3-6). This shows that companies' access to working capital and investment financing has become costly and restricted, and that households are postponing consumer credit use (especially housing/vehicle). Retail sales rising %1,4 monthly and %10,1 annually in August, while showing nominal growth, indicate a contraction of around %15-16 in real terms (deflated by inflation). Industrial production contracting -%1,0 monthly and -%1,86 annually and capacity utilization stuck at %74,5 indicate that the combination of domestic demand pressure and external demand uncertainty (EU industry -%1,1) is delaying the investment decision process. The credit channel and interest rate channel are operating clearly in the "restrictive" zone with these data; however, the sustainability of this restrictiveness is being tested by the expansionary course of budget policy (detailed below) running in the opposite direction.

en:f5aa02763f6d24dfd38e: The Türkiye economy shows with the September 2026 data that the disinflation process is at its "mid-advanced stage", but stands at a critical junction regarding the process's hardest part, the "last mile" (approach to the single-digit target) and the timing of normalizing (cutting) the policy rate. According to TÜİK data, September CPI fell to annual %29,73 (previous %31,51), monthly %1,84 (below the %2,3 forecast); PPI too preserved its improvement trend at annual %27,38 (previous %27,95), monthly %2,07 (previous %2,57). These data indicate that the tight monetary policy built with the TCMB's %37 policy rate (Real rate: policy rate minus 12-month-forward inflation ~ around +7-8 points of positive real rate) works through the demand channel (suppressing domestic demand) and the expectations channel (decline in inflation expectations), and that it also suppresses imported inflation based on the Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) index's slight appreciation to 105,45 in September (previous 105,0). Growth dynamics reflect the cost of this tightness: while 2026/Q2 GDP grew annually %2,3 (below the %2,9 forecast), quarterly %1,1; industrial production ran annually -%1,86, monthly -%1,0 in August, revealing that the production side has come under the pressure of rate sensitivity and real credit costs (deposit rate %43,04, consumer loan rate %64,74). The capacity utilization rate staying relatively stable at %74,5 in October (previous %74,2), the end of the inventory cycle and support from external demand (exports 25,98 bn USD in September, previous 23,47 bn) suggest that investment delays have not yet led to a deep contraction. In the labor market, the August unemployment rate at %7,7 and the economic participation rate at %52,5 show the contraction's effect on employment is still controlled; however, retail sales contracting seriously in real terms (annually %10,1 nominal vs %29,73 inflation) and the consumer confidence index staying below the optimistic/pessimistic threshold (100) at 91,9 points in September (previous 90,8) reveal that household perception is still fragile. In summary; while Türkiye has achieved success in "stability indicators" such as inflation falling below %29,73, the current account turning to surplus (+4,05 bn USD in August) and reserves increasing (64,57 bn USD), it is living through the hardest point of the "growth-inflation trade-off" with growth pulled below potential, industry contracting and real rates staying high.

However, the sustainability of this balance depends on the consistency of fiscal policy with monetary policy (policy mix consistency), the course of global energy prices (Brent 113 USD risk) and how the "hawkish" shift in the Fed's rate path will affect emerging markets through risk appetite. The explosion of the budget deficit in the September data (532 mld TL) constitutes the largest domestic risk factor (fiscal dominance) for the coming period; financing this deficit without money printing (domestic borrowing / reserve use) is the critical condition that will keep real interest rates high and thus sustain disinflation. The sudden cooling in global risk appetite (VIX 20) and the structural resistance in long-term US yields (30Y %5,29) indicate that foreign portfolio flows will remain selective and fragile. BIST 30 valuations have priced in the current rate-peak expectation and slow disinflation; however, "earnings momentum" is negative in the industrial and retail sectors and neutral/positive in banking (CPI linker portfolio effect). In the coming period, whether the stickiness of inflation in the services component (rent, restaurants, transport) breaks, how the Treasury's year-end cash need is met, and the direction of the Fed's December "dot plot" update will be the main catalysts determining the performance of Türkiye assets (TL, Bonds, BIST). Однако продолжение геополитических рисков (напряжённость Иран — Ближний Восток) и колебаний цен на энергоносители (цены на природный газ выше 71 €/MWh) остаётся фактором давления особенно на энергоёмкие и подверженные геополитическим рискам секторы. Неопределённость относительно сентябрьского решения Fed по ставке и опасения глобальной рецессии снижают аппетит к риску и приводят к оттоку капитала в более безопасные активы. В этой среде основная перспектива управления фондом — ставя во главу угла хеджирование риска высокой долей наличных, продолжать формировать контролируемые позиции в отобранных акциях с сильной технической и фундаментальной устойчивостью. Рынок, ожидая с одной стороны решения Fed по ставке, с другой — должен быть готов к волатильности, создаваемой геополитическими рисками.

Банковский сектор с акциями VAKBN, YKBNK, GARAN, AKBNK и ISCTR испытывает полное давление «СИЛЬНО ПРОДАВАТЬ». У всех этих акций технические индикаторы слабые, наблюдается потеря импульса, а доходность за 60 дней у большинства ниже 20%, у некоторых даже видны потери до 25%. Сектор находится под давлением из-за опасений, что высокая инфляция негативно повлияет на спрос на кредиты и качество активов. Аналогично энергетический и нефтехимический сектор показывает слабость с акциями ASTOR, PETKM, ENKAI и TUPRS. В частности, ASTOR привлекает внимание драматической потерей стоимости на 18.10% за последние 5 дней. В группе холдингов (KCHOL, SAHOL) также преобладают сигналы «ПРОДАВАТЬ» и «СИЛЬНО ПРОДАВАТЬ». Единственным исключением в этой общей среде слабости является BIMAS (BİM). BIMAS, в отличие от всех других акций, подаёт сигнал «НЕЙТРАЛЬНО». Розничный сектор демонстрирует относительную устойчивость из-за стабильности потребительского спроса и сопротивляемости инфляции. Другие секторы — оборонный, автомобильный, телекоммуникационный, недвижимости и авиационный — поскольку почти полностью закрылись с сигналами «СИЛЬНО ПРОДАВАТЬ», тоже получили свою долю риска, распространившегося на весь рынок. Это подчёркивает, что при формировании портфеля отраслевое распределение приобретает критическую важность и следует избегать портфелей с преобладанием финансов и энергетики.

RSI 68,05 и положительное положение MACD показывают, что акция вошла в зону перекупленности, но сильный тренд продолжается. zh:04ca602c3c1562aa9e99: 货币政策对内需的传导渠道（transmission channels）正通过所提供的数据得到具体体现。TCMB 借助政策利率（%37）与流动性窗口利率构成的"利率走廊"，决定着银行体系的成本结构。10 月数据显示 TL 存款利率为 %43,04（此前 %43,80），8 月数据显示消费贷款利率为 %64,74（此前 %63,67）；这表明实际存款利率（以年通胀 %29,73 计算，约为 %43,04-11）和实际贷款利率（约 %27-28）显著为正。这一高实际成本使 M3 货币供应增速（10 月年率 %28,65，此前 %29,78）落后于名义通胀（%29,73），从而导致实际货币供应（real M3）持续收缩。与弗里德曼"通货膨胀无论何时何地都是一种货币现象"的论断相一致，实际货币供应的收缩正在侵蚀社会持有的购买力，并抑制总需求（aggregate demand）。银行贷款年增速 %36,32（8 月，此前 %36,60）名义上看似仍然很高；但经通胀平减后，实际信贷增长已降至个位数（约 %2,3-6）水平。这表明企业获取营运资金和投资融资的渠道变得成本高昂且受限，家庭也在推迟消费信贷（尤其是住房/汽车）的使用。8 月零售销售月率增长 %1,4、年率增长 %10,1，名义上虽有增长，但按实际值（经 CPI 平减）计算，收缩幅度约在 %15-16 左右。工业生产月率 -%1,0、年率 -%1,86 的收缩，加上产能利用率停留在 %74,5，表明内需压力与外需不确定性（EU 工业 -%1,1）的叠加正在推迟投资决策（investment decision）过程。根据这些数据，信贷渠道（credit channel）和利率渠道（interest rate channel）明确运行于"限制性"（restrictive）区间；但这种限制性的可持续性，正因其走向与财政政策（下文详述）的扩张方向相反而受到考验。

zh:f5627365701c964d4107: 货币政策向内需的传导渠道（transmission channels）正随着所提供的数据具体化。TCMB 通过政策利率（%37）和流动性窗口利率构建的“利率走廊”，决定着银行体系的成本结构。以 10 月数据，TL 存款利率运行于 %43,04（前值 %43,80）；以 8 月数据，消费贷款利率 %64,74（前值 %63,67）；这表明实际存款利率（以年度通胀 %29,73 为基准约 %43,04-11）和实际贷款利率（约 %27-28）显著为正。这一高实际成本，导致 M3 货币供应量增长（10 月年度 %28,65、前值 %29,78）落后于名义通胀（%29,73），从而使实际货币供应量（real M3）持续收缩。实际货币供应量的收缩，与弗里德曼“通货膨胀在任何时候和任何地方都是一种货币现象”的论断一致，正在侵蚀社会的购买力并压制总需求（aggregate demand）。银行贷款年度增长 %36,32（8月、前值 %36,60）在名义上看似仍高；但经通胀平减后，实际信贷增长已降至个位数（约 %2,3-6）。这表明企业获得营运资金和投资融资的渠道已变得昂贵且受限，家庭也在推迟消费信贷（尤其是住房/汽车）的使用。8 月零售销售月度增长 %1,4、年度 %10,1，虽显示名义增长，但实际（经通胀平减）表明约 %15-16 的收缩。工业生产月度 -%1,0、年度 -%1,86 的收缩，以及产能利用率卡在 %74,5，表明内需压力与外需不确定性（欧盟工业 -%1,1）的组合正在推迟投资决策过程。信贷渠道与利率渠道正以这些数据清晰地运行于“限制性”区域；但这一限制性的可持续性，正受到预算政策（下文详述）扩张走向反向运行的检验。

zh:f5aa02763f6d24dfd38e: 以 2026 年 9 月数据来看，Türkiye（图尔基耶）经济表明去通胀进程处于“中后段”，但在该进程最艰难的部分——“最后一英里”（接近个位数目标）以及政策利率正常化（降息）时点上，正处关键十字路口。据 TÜİK 数据，9 月 CPI 年度降至 %29,73（前值 %31,51）、月度 %1,84（低于 %2,3 预测）；PPI 亦保持改善趋势，年度 %27,38（前值 %27,95）、月度 %2,07（前值 %2,57）。这些数据表明，TCMB 以 %37 政策利率构建的紧缩货币政策（实际利率：政策利率减 12 个月前瞻通胀，约 +7-8 个点的正实际利率），通过需求渠道（抑制内需）和预期渠道（通胀预期回落）发挥作用；同时基于实际有效汇率（REER）指数 9 月小幅升值至 105,45（前值 105,0），也压制了输入型通胀。增长动态则反映紧缩的代价：2026/Q2 GDP 年度增长 %2,3（低于 %2,9 预测）、季度 %1,1；工业生产 8 月年度 -%1,86、月度 -%1,0 运行，显示生产端已进入利率敏感性和实际信贷成本（存款利率 %43,04、消费贷款利率 %64,74）的压力之下。产能利用率 10 月相对稳定于 %74,5（前值 %74,2）、库存周期结束以及外部需求（9 月出口 25,98 mld USD、前值 23,47 mld）的支持，暗示投资延迟尚未导致深度收缩。就业市场上，8 月失业率 %7,7、经济参与率 %52,5 运行，表明收缩对就业的影响仍可控；但零售销售实际口径（年度 %10,1 名义 vs %29,73 通胀）显著收缩，消费者信心指数 9 月以 91,9 点（前值 90,8）停留在乐观/悲观阈值（100）之下，显示家庭感知仍然脆弱。概言之；Türkiye 在“稳定指标”上取得成绩——通胀降至 %29,73 以下、经常账户转为顺差（8 月 +4,05 mld USD）、储备增加（64,57 mld USD）——但同时以增长被拉至潜在之下、工业收缩、实际利率居高，正在经历“增长-通胀权衡”的最艰难时点。
